learning_outcomes.text: Students will have broad knowledge in the field of modern metallic materials and their systematic selection.
Students will acquire in-depth knowledge to interpret the relationships between structure, processing, and properties of materials.
Students will be able to analyze material-related data.

These qualifications enable students to make informed decisions in the selection of sustainable materials and effectively integrate insights from previous modules. Decisions will be substantiated using calculation tools if necessary.
Students will be able to select suitable materials for technical applications based on a systematic stress analysis, supported by calculation tools if necessary.

The acquired knowledge can foster innovation by stimulating thought about alternative materials and technologies, thus opening new possibilities for the development of innovative products and technologies.
Students will prepare results obtained from practical experiments and calculations in a team.
Subsequently, the results will be discussed and communicated in an appropriate form, considering the learned material and supplementary technical literature.

syllabus_topics: Selection of construction materials considering sustainability aspects
teaching_methods: Workshops on calculation and simulation tools
assessment_rules: The presentation (with written elaboration) will cover topics based on the content taught in the lecture and accounts for 70% of the grade. The homework, which relates to calculation tasks, tests competencies in using simulation tools for sustainable material selection and accounts for 30% of the grade. The 'experimental work' refers to the conducted laboratory experiments and is an ungraded assessment. The presentation will be approximately 20 minutes with an elaboration of about 10 pages. The homework will be approximately 10 pages.
